messages:
marta: heads up — observed 95th percentile generation latency spike when fallback routing hit hosted->dedicated split last night. apps saw cold-starts of 7-9s.

alex: ugh. was that the preemptible burst nodes we routed to?

marta: yes. routing policy sent ~30% traffic to dedicated-preemptible in eu-west-1 while primary hosted pool was degraded. those nodes are fine for throughput but cold-boot time kills SLO.

jia: quick data: from logs the sequence is: request lands -> provision pod -> kube-scheduler picks GPU node -> container pulls model layer -> runtime warms kv cache. provisioning dominates.

sam: can you paste the pod annotation we used for routing? and the node taint setup?

marta: here is the current pod annotation we use for forced routing: 
```yaml
metadata:
  annotations:
    redwood.routing/prefer_pool: "dedicated-preemptible"
```
nodes are tainted: `node.kubernetes.io/gpu_preemptible=true:NoSchedule` and we allow pods with toleration to land there.

kevin: tolerations + annotation feels brittle. a namespace-level guard might be safer so we avoid random service pods landing in preemptible pools.

alex: agreed. namespace annotation + webhook admission that injects toleration only for namespaces with `redwood/pool=preemptible` would reduce accidental moves. also helps with chargeback mapping.

jia: tradeoff: namespace pinning increases isolation but reduces flexibility for short bursts. if we pin too strictly, autoscaler can't spread temporary spikes across pools.

sam: cost note: preemptible nodes are ~60% cheaper but have higher cold-start penalty. for CPU-bound embed jobs it's fine, for generation latency SLOs not great.

marta: proposal: 3-part policy
1) default namespaces get `redwood/pool=hosted` (no tolerations injected)
2) tenant namespaces opt-in with `redwood/pool=preemptible` to enable tolerations and quota counters
3) admission webhook enforces pod-level `maxStartupDelay` label for critical pods -> disallow scheduling to preemptible when label is `critical`

alex: +1 on webhook. also add cluster-autoscaler profiling: prefer scale-up of warm nodes for pools serving low-latency workloads using `--balance-similar-node-groups=false`? might be risky.

kevin: another idea: maintain a small warm buffer (1-2 nodes) in each dedicated pool for low-latency tiers. cost impact small vs SLA hit.

oncall-bot: INCIDENT-1978891234: latency spike detected 2026-03-05T02:14:22Z — routed to dedicated-preemptible — severity low — auto-closed by team.

sam: action items
- jia: prototype admission webhook and namespace annotation schema (ETA 2 days)
- kevin: quantify cost of 1-node warm buffer per region (ETA 3 days)
- marta: instrument more fine-grained telemetry for pod provision time (ETA 24h)

alex: can we add a quick `kubectl` snippet to detect pods currently tolerating preemptible taint?

marta: yup: `kubectl get pods -A -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.namespace}//{.metadata.name}//{.spec.tolerations}{"\n"}{end}' | grep preemptible`

kevin: thanks — will sync after data. :thumbsup:

marta: thanks team — will put PR for webhook schema in #eng-releases when ready. :rocket:
